title: Best Card Grading Company (2026)
verdict: AGS is the best card grading company in 2026 for collectors who want a grade they can verify: every card is laser-measured, given eight subgrades and returned in 20 business days or less for a flat $18.

The caveat is resale. PSA holders bring more money on most cards, and that will not change quickly. Grade with PSA when the premium beats its fee and its wait. Grade with AGS when you want the facts about the card, fast, at a price that ignores what it is worth.

list: Pull the one or two cards you will auction. If PSA's premium on them beats its fee and wait, send those to PSA.
Send the rest to a flat-fee grader. At AGS that is $18 a card, or $15 from 30 TCG cards.
Leave out commons and damaged cards unless you want them protected.
Read the reports when the cards come back. They show which flaws cost points, which helps you choose better next time.

why: Human grading is a judgment made in seconds, and it varies. AGS replaces the judgment with a measurement: a 3D laser maps the card, software scores centering, corners, edges and surface, and the grade follows from the numbers. That is why AGS says a regrade rarely moves.

You see why the card got its grade. AGS issues eight subgrades, four for the front and four for the back, plus a defect list and a 3D heightmap. Most graders hand back one number. A buyer who can open the report has less to argue about.

One price covers everything. $18 buys the scan, the grade, eight subgrades, the report and the slab, for any card at any value. Orders of 30 or more TCG cards pay $15 a card on the standard bulk tier.

faq.q: What is the best card grading company?
faq.a: For a measured, repeatable grade with a full report at a flat price, AGS. For the highest resale price on a valuable card, PSA. For the lowest fee from a large grader, CGC.

faq.q: Does grading increase a card's value?
faq.a: Often, not always. A high grade on a card in demand can multiply its price. A low grade can sell for less than the raw card. Look at sold prices for the grade you realistically expect.

faq.q: How much does AGS charge to grade a card?
faq.a: $18 per card at the standard rate, whatever the card is worth. Bulk orders of 30 or more TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 or $30 at 5. Sports and non-TCG bulk is $3 more per tier.

faq.q: What grading scale does AGS use?
faq.a: 1 to 10 with decimal precision. An AGS 10 is near-perfect measurable condition. A 9.5 has minor flaws that do not significantly affect condition.

faq.q: How do I verify an AGS slab?
faq.a: Enter the cert number from the label on agscard.com. The record shows the grade and the scan report for that card.
